items.stem: Read instructions from a household management book (1845): ‘The mistress of a household should rise early, for it is impossible that her servants should be punctual if she is not. The breakfast-table must be laid by eight o’clock. Let the kitchen be inspected daily, and let no waste be suffered. Whilst the lady need not herself perform menial tasks, she ought to understand them, that she may judge whether they are well done.’ Analyse how this text differs from present-day English in lexis, grammar, orthography and discourse, and explain the reasons for the differences.
items.answer: Indicative content: ‘should rise early’ (modal verb of obligation): deontic modals (should, must, ought to) give advice with moral authority; ‘Let the kitchen be inspected daily’ (let + passive imperative): an indirect, impersonal command structure now rare; ‘let no waste be suffered’ (semantic change): ‘suffered’ means ‘allowed’, a sense now archaic; ‘Whilst the lady’ (conjunction now declining): ‘whilst’ is declining in frequency in favour of ‘while’; ‘that she may judge’ (subjunctive / archaic purpose clause): ‘that she may’ for ‘so that she can’ is now formal; ‘breakfast-table’ (hyphenated compound): compounds often begin hyphenated and later close up or open (‘breakfast table’); ‘her servants’ (social context): reference to servants reflects the class structure of Victorian households; context: 1845, before/after standardisation; modern version: Householders should get up early: staff will not be punctual otherwise. Breakfast must be laid by eight. Check the kitchen every day and do not allow waste …

A word acquiring a more negative meaning
items.answer: A word acquiring a more positive meaning over time

items.stem: The following words have entered English in the 21st century: ‘staycation’, ‘hangry’, ‘vlog’. Analyse how each was formed and evaluate what these words suggest about the causes of lexical change today.
items.answer: ‘staycation’: blending (stay + vacation). ‘hangry’: blending (hungry + angry). ‘vlog’: blending/clipping (video + blog). They reflect technology, social media and changing social practices.
